answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a small, time-locked stake that is slashed on proven fraud. Before an agent may act, it must present a cipher-based proof binding its key to a unique hardware or payment credential, so one operator cannot cheaply forge thousands of lookalike accounts. Reputation then accrues slowly through attested work, and reaching the summit of trust takes weeks of consistent behavior, making a mass fake-identity attack expensive in both money and time while honest newcomers can still join with a modest deposit.
